key_insight: GBClaw connects agentic AI-driven simulations with mechanistic analysis, revealing how defect hierarchies and metastable grain-boundary structures influence sliding resistance.
engineering_relevance: Understanding deformation at general grain boundaries can inform microstructure design aimed at controlling interfacial strength in polycrystalline materials.
method: Integrate LLMs with an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory.
Use dynamic replanning to connect systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis.
Compare sliding with and without secondary grain-boundary misfit dislocations, then investigate anomalies through researcher-guided calculations.
evidence_signal: Across 14 general asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, GBClaw identified diverse deformation modes and substantial shear-strength differences associated with secondary misfit dislocations.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the studied nickel boundaries, and investigation of anomalous resistance required researcher-guided follow-up.
paper_title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
